questions.explain: Explicit preferences have confidence 1.0; inferred start at 0.6, gain 0.1 per observation week, and are capped at 0.9 — never reaching 1.0, which is reserved for explicit statements.
options: Both start at 1.0
Inferred preferences are always more trusted
Explicit preferences expire faster
Explicit = confidence 1.0; inferred starts at 0.6, capped at 0.9, never reaching 1.0
questions.q: How do explicit and inferred preferences differ in confidence?

questions.explain: Inference promotes only after ≥3 independent observations AND no conflicting explicit preference on the same key — the two gates before an inferred preference is stored.
options: ≥3 independent observations and no conflicting explicit preference
A single observation is enough
Only on weekends
Whenever the model feels confident
questions.q: What are the two gates for promoting an inferred preference?

questions.explain: Priority: explicit always beats inferred; newer explicit beats older explicit (supersede, don't delete); contradictory inferred preferences decay each other.
options: Inferred beats explicit when confidence is higher
Oldest preference always wins
Explicit beats inferred always; newer explicit beats older explicit; contradictory inferred decay each other
Conflicts are resolved by deleting both
questions.q: What are the conflict-resolution rules for preferences?

questions.explain: Active preferences compile via STRING_AGG into a compact per-category block costing 30–60 tokens — the highest-ROI tokens in the prompt — with inferred preferences gated at confidence ≥0.7.
options: Append all preferences verbatim to every prompt
Compile active preferences into a compact cached profile block (30–60 tokens), gating inferred ones at confidence ≥0.7
Send preferences to a separate LLM call
Store preferences only in the client
questions.q: How are preferences injected into the prompt efficiently?

questions.explain: Show users what was inferred with confirm/dismiss (dismissal blocks re-inference for 90 days), offer category-level opt-out, and cover preferences in GDPR export/delete — plus TTLs since tastes change.
options: Inference should be invisible to users
Preferences never expire
Consent is not needed for inferred data
A visible "what the assistant knows" page, per-key dismissal with 90-day cooling-off, opt-out, and preference expiry/TTLs
questions.q: What does the chapter's consent and expiry model require?
